audits.title: P-EGS30 Audit of the management of patients presenting with gallstone pancreatitis during the COVID-19 pandemic
audits.standard: BSG guidelines: ERCP within 72h of pain onset; cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge

cycle1.period: March to August 2020 compared with the same period in 2019
cycle1.result: Significant differences between COVID and pre-COVID groups, especially fewer hot procedures and fewer patients receiving definitive treatment during COVID; pre-COVID results similar to 2016 audit, in which 76% received definitive treatment.

audits.other_findings: Most ERCP delays were due to the weekend effect; 16 of the 40 patients without definitive treatment re-presented with biliary flares or pancreatitis within a year.
audits.citation: Thomas C, Hutchinson K, Brown J. P-EGS30 Audit of the management of patients presenting with gallstone pancreatitis during the COVID-19 pandemic. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab430.090.

audits.title: 211 A Snapshot Audit of Time to Intervention for Gallstone Pancreatitis During the First Wave of COVID-19
audits.standard: BSG guidelines: definitive management of gallstone pancreatitis during index admission or within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: Non-COVID 2019 cohort: 30% (n = 7 of 23) had definitive management within index admission or 2 weeks; first-wave COVID-19 2020 cohort: 64.7% (n = 11 of 17).

audits.other_findings: Patients not treated within 2 weeks during COVID-19 waited longer and had more readmissions.
audits.citation: O'Halloran R, Coulson R, Magee C. 211 A Snapshot Audit of Time to Intervention for Gallstone Pancreatitis During the First Wave of COVID-19. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.131.

audits.title: 262 Full Cycle Audit on Definitive Management of Biliary Pancreatitis
audits.standard: BSG guidelines: definitive management of mild gallstone pancreatitis on the same admission or within 2 weeks

cycle1.result: All suitable patients had timely cholecystectomy.

cycle2.result: None of the 4 patients had cholecystectomy within 2 weeks.

audits.other_findings: The fall was attributed to the COVID-19 elective backlog; all patients eventually had surgery.
audits.citation: Islam R, Hashmi Z, Aljarad F, Madanur M, Imtiaz N, Warren R. 262 Full Cycle Audit on Definitive Management of Biliary Pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.170.

audits.title: FTP5.7 Championing Benign Biliary Patients in a UGI Tertiary Referral Cancer Centre. Results from a 3 year Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Key performance indicators: time to Lap-C, rate of Lap-C within 2 weeks after pancreatitis, inpatient Lap-C rate, outpatient appointments saved
audits.setting: UGI tertiary referral cancer centre, Guy's & St Thomas' NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 27%; average time to Lap-C 68 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 2%.

audits.intervention: Dedicated consultant-led biliary service, live biliary admission tracking system, increased inpatient Lap-C, ambulatory pathways and integrated care approach.

cycle2.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 69% (41% as inpatients); average time to Lap-C 13 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 19% for fit and consenting patients.

audits.other_findings: 103 outpatient appointments saved (£12360) by counselling and pre-assessing as inpatients; project followed 3 earlier audit cycles.
audits.citation: Forsyth K, Johnson R, Boghdady M, Wheatstone S, Tomasi I, Knight W, et al.. FTP5.7 Championing Benign Biliary Patients in a UGI Tertiary Referral Cancer Centre. Results from a 3 year Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.378.

audits.title: 1268 An Audit of the Time to Surgery Following Diagnosis of Gallstone Pancreatitis
audits.standard: BSG guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within 2 weeks of discharge

cycle1.result: 14 (67%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 9 (64%) of these within 2 weeks; 7 (33%) had no surgery; median wait 3 days, average 64 days; 6 readmissions while waiting.

audits.intervention: Weekly semi-emergency theatre list introduced; re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: Of those not operated, 4 were not eligible, 1 went private and 2 were awaiting surgery; pain was the commonest readmission reason.
audits.citation: Sekyi-Djan M, Agnihotri A, Goian L. 1268 An Audit of the Time to Surgery Following Diagnosis of Gallstone Pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.194.

audits.title: HPB O08 Championing benign biliary patients in Emergency General Surgery: A 3 year quality improvement project
audits.standard: Biliary key performance indicators: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 2 weeks of pancreatitis, time to Lap-C, inpatient Lap-C rate
audits.setting: Emergency general surgery, Guy's and St Thomas', London

cycle1.result: 2-week Lap-C after pancreatitis 27%; average time to Lap-C 68 days; inpatient Lap-C rate 2%.

audits.intervention: Consultant-led biliary service, live biliary patient tracking system, increased inpatient Lap-C, ambulatory pathways and integrated care approach.

cycle2.result: 2-week Lap-C 79% (43% as inpatients); average time to Lap-C 13 days; inpatient Lap-C 19%.

audits.other_findings: Three earlier audit cycles showed delays; 191 outpatient appointments saved (£22920).

audits.title: EP551 - Assessment of Surgical Management for Mild and Moderate Acute Gallstone Pancreatitis in Accordance with AUGIS Guidelines: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks for surgically fit patients with mild to moderate gallstone pancreatitis
audits.setting: Single surgical unit, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.result: 19 (16.5%) had inpatient cholecystectomy, 42 (36.5%) outpatient cholecystectomy, 4 (3.5%) declined, 10 (8.7%) unfit; no documented reason in 40 (34.8%).

audits.other_findings: Median length of stay 5.8 days; median Charlson index 4.5 in those with no documented reason.
audits.citation: Tan E, Ng S, Ismail M, Khan K. EP551 - Assessment of Surgical Management for Mild and Moderate Acute Gallstone Pancreatitis in Accordance with AUGIS Guidelines: A Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.515.

audits.title: BN SO13 - Re-Audit of Biliary Pancreatitis Management: Enhancing Compliance with Timely Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
audits.standard: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission for biliary acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: General surgery department, Northampton General Hospital

cycle2.result: 64.5% had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within two weeks of admission.

audits.other_findings: Persistent barriers: limited ultrasound slots, insufficient hot gallbladder lists, pre-assessment clinics and reluctance to perform acute laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
audits.citation: Sakr M, Methany R. BN SO13 - Re-Audit of Biliary Pancreatitis Management: Enhancing Compliance with Timely Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae271.184.

audits.title: 422 Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Gallstone Pancreatitis – Audit and Improvement of Trust Performance
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: index or early (within 2 weeks) cholecystectomy for mild gallstone pancreatitis; delayed surgery for moderate/severe
audits.intervention: Listing gallstone pancreatitis patients as P2 when booking, cancelling other elective activity when required, and encouraging inpatient cholecystectomy.
audits.other_findings: Median length of stay for index cholecystectomy rose from 3 to 6 days (p<0.05), attributed to CEPOD theatre access; non-compliance linked to poor documentation and slow outpatient processing.
audits.citation: Ugur S, Tol I, Scout E, Rao S. 422 Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Gallstone Pancreatitis – Audit and Improvement of Trust Performance. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.040.

audits.title: TPTh 9.09 Audit of the Timing of Cholecystectomy in Gallstone-Induced Pancreatitis: Adherence to Guidelines and Impact on Patient Outcomes
audits.standard: National guidelines: cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge

cycle1.result: 30 (50.8%) operated; 9 (15.2%) timely; mean delay 11.2 weeks; 19 (32%) readmitted, 10 with recurrent GIP.

audits.intervention: Expedited cholecystectomy pathway and live tracker.

cycle2.result: 15 operated (50%); 13 (43%) timely, 12 during index admission and 1 within 2 weeks of discharge.

audits.other_findings: Root causes were lack of structured follow-up, delays in anaesthetic clearance and limited theatre availability.
audits.citation: Sajol M, El-Salahi M, Arshad M, Sharaf U. TPTh 9.09 Audit of the Timing of Cholecystectomy in Gallstone-Induced Pancreatitis: Adherence to Guidelines and Impact on Patient Outcomes. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.524.

audits.title: TPW 7.13 Audit into the Management of Gallstone Pancreatitis at A Tertiary Care NHS Trust
audits.standard: NICE: cholecystectomy during index admission or within two weeks of discharge for non-severe gallstone pancreatitis
audits.setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust, Brighton

cycle1.result: Of 30 mild or moderate cases, 2 (6.6%) had cholecystectomy during index admission; of 14 (45%) with elective surgery within five months, 2 (14%) were within two weeks.

audits.intervention: Planned dedicated hot cholecystectomy pathway with protected theatre capacity and re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Delays due to uncertain fitness (4), awaiting MRCP (6) and awaiting ERCP (3); 3 (10.7%) readmitted with recurrent biliary pathology.
audits.citation: Lam W, Alsardia Y, Khan N, Mohamed M, Magsi A, Athansiou A. TPW 7.13 Audit into the Management of Gallstone Pancreatitis at A Tertiary Care NHS Trust. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.382.
